findings.description: Fallback to unverified TLS context when fetching package metadata from PyPI
findings.code_snippet:
def _request_context():
    yield None
    # fallback to non verified HTTPS (the information we request is not sensitive, so fallback)
    yield ssl._create_unverified_context()  # noqa: S323, SLF001
...
with urlopen(url, context=context) as file_handler:  # noqa: S310
findings.reasoning: _request_context() yields a verified context first, but on URLError it retries with ssl._create_unverified_context(). Any URLError (including a TLS certificate verification failure caused by a MITM) triggers the unverified retry, so an on-path attacker can serve forged PyPI JSON metadata. The data is used to pick the version of wheels to install (periodic update), so spoofed metadata can influence which packages are seeded into new environments. The code comment argues the data is not sensitive, but integrity is also at stake, not only confidentiality.

evidence.code_context: _request_context yields None (verified) then ssl._create_unverified_context(); _pypi_get_distribution_info loops over contexts and calls urlopen(url, context=context) for https://pypi.org/pypi/{distribution}/json, breaking only on success.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: Not traced with the tool. The fallback is structural: the second yield is reached whenever the first attempt raises URLError.
evidence.notes: Realistic exploitability depends on network position (MITM). Impact is integrity of metadata used for wheel selection.

findings.description: zipfile extractall flagged as zip slip; mitigated by CPython zipfile path sanitization and trusted wheel source
findings.code_snippet:
with zipfile.ZipFile(str(self._wheel)) as zip_ref:
    self._shorten_path_if_needed(zip_ref)
    zip_ref.extractall(str(self._image_dir))
findings.reasoning: zipfile.ZipFile.extractall sanitizes member names: it strips absolute prefixes and drops '..' components, so entries cannot escape _image_dir. The wheel comes from virtualenv's bundled wheels or the app data cache, which are not attacker-controlled in normal use. Residual risk is limited to a malicious wheel supplied by the user, which is outside the trust boundary.

evidence.notes: Zip-slip via extractall is not exploitable on supported CPython versions.

findings.description: zipfile extraction of bundled wheel to destination path
findings.code_snippet:
def extract(full_path, dest):
    sub_file = _get_path_within_zip(full_path)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(ROOT, "r") as zip_file:
        info = zip_file.getinfo(sub_file)
        info.filename = dest.name
        zip_file.extract(info, str(dest.parent))
findings.reasoning: Source paths are resolved with realpath and must start with the archive root prefix, otherwise an error is raised. The member filename is overwritten with dest.name, which removes any directory components from the archive entry name, so zip-slip via member names is not possible. The archive is the package's own bundled ROOT, not attacker-supplied.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: Archive is ROOT (bundled package). Member name is overwritten with dest.name before extraction.
evidence.notes: Not exploitable by an external attacker.
